claims.summary: In the dimension-four characteristic-zero Taylor setup, for every d>=2 and every two-pair collision stratum Z, the primitive forms F=Delta/u, m1=M_(N-1)/u and k=K/u all belong to I_Z^[d(d-1)] in the local ring at the generic point of Z, where N=8d-4 and u=c(e4 V)^[d^2+(d-1)^2].
claims.assessment: Working proof using a regular four-conic smoothing, an explicit vertical twist, the section-lattice index from Euler characteristics and torsion cohomology, and parity. This proves only a lower bound: equality, tangent cones, colon lengths and first-step thresholds remain open.
claims.rationale: A uniform lower half of the two-pair order conjecture replaces low-degree evidence on this part of the first-step route. It does not settle any full open statement; novelty is not claimed.
claims.next_action: Determine the remaining torsion length or a matching Taylor-minor upper bound in the same degeneration, retaining the original section lattice.

relationships: Uses the exact common collision factor to pass from raw Taylor determinants to primitive forms.
Uses triangular transport of the primitive triple and transitivity on two-pair strata.
The one-pair extension obstruction warns against replacing extending sections by central node matching.
Proves the lower order inequality only; equality, tangent-cone factors and triple nonvanishing remain conjectural.
The ramification budget motivated specialization, but is not used to infer local orders.

conj:cube-two-pair-order.mathematical_status: The new characteristic-zero theorem proves only order at least d(d-1); the exact order, tangent cones and triple-stratum statement remain conjectural.

conj:cube-two-pair-order.assessment: Conjecture. The lower bound d(d-1) for all three primitive forms at every two-pair stratum is now proved in characteristic zero by thm:cube-two-pair-order-lower-bound. Matching upper bounds, the asserted tangent-cone factors and the triple-stratum assertion remain open; retained modular d=2,3,4 data support but do not prove them.
